create.name: Adelaide Ashtanga Yoga Shala
create.bio:
Adelaide Ashtanga Yoga Shala is an Ashtanga school on Magill Road in Stepney, Adelaide, run by the married teachers Youngblood and Maura Roche. Both hold level 2 authorisation in the Ashtanga method. Youngblood has practised for more than twenty-five years and studied over many trips to Mysore with Sri K. Pattabhi Jois and later with R. Sharath Jois; Maura came to Ashtanga from ballet, athletics and strength training, met Youngblood in Mysore, and has also taught movement to dancers of the Australian Dance Theatre.

The core of the timetable is a traditional Mysore programme on weekday and Sunday mornings, in which each student works through the series independently with individual guidance; newcomers commit to at least a month. Around it sit evening and weekend classes, among them a Primary Series class named after Patanjali and several dynamic flow classes themed on figures such as Shiva, Hanuman and Nataraja. Classes can be joined in the room or online, with live and recorded sessions included in the shala's yearly membership, and a smaller sister shala at Carrickalinga runs music-led Ashtanga flow classes on Fridays and Sundays. The website also shares the opening and closing chants with their Sanskrit text and translation.

courses.title: Weekly classes and pricing
courses.description: The weekly timetable of Mysore, led Primary and flow classes, paid by trial pass, drop-in, class card or monthly unlimited pass.
courses.price: 2-Week Trial Pass (Unlimited) $45 (available for all non-Mysore classes); Drop-in (IN-SHALA Only) $29; 4 class card (4-wk Expiry) $105; 10 class card (5-wk Expiry) $225; Monthly (Unlimited) $250

courses.title: Infinity Plan membership
courses.description: A rolling twelve-month membership with unlimited access to in-shala classes and to the live and recorded online classes, with holds and two weeks' notice to leave.

free_resources.title: Opening and Closing Chants
free_resources.description: The traditional Ashtanga opening and closing chants, set out in Sanskrit script, in transliteration and in English translation for students learning them.
